text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS
- Half of civil servants at Martutene prison want to leave after prison worker shot dead in ETA attack.
- Government, with support of votes from United Left (IU), passes new digital television law through Congress.
EL MUNDO
- Photos of two Belgian soldiers torturing Somalia child published.
- Telefonica and BT create one of world communication giants.
DIARIO 16
- Terror in prisons after ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) targets workers.
- Government passes digital television law with support of IU against Prisa and Antena 3 and in favour of its friends.
ABC
- Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar says structural reforms will ensure social peace and create jobs.
CINCO DIAS
- Iberia, Spanair and Air Europa increase prices by 30 percent.
- BBV attributed profit grows by 25 percent in first quarter.
- Sale of last 10 percent of Repsol will be most successful in terms of retail demand
- Only 1.7 percent of contracts created in 1996 were permanent, according to INE.
EXPANSION
- Stock market reaches historic highs.
- Telefonica will sign alliance with BT-MCI today.
- Alvaro Declaux, father of Cosme held by ETA, says Vidrala will not pay ransom for son.
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Government makes conditions for bankruptcy and stock market suspensions harder.
